name: Etizolam
meta: Schedule H – prescription only; regulated as a controlled psychotropic in several
sections: White to pale yellowish crystalline powder.
A thienotriazolodiazepine marketed in Japan, Italy and India; not approved in the USA or UK. First approval/introduction: Patented 1972; approved in Japan 1984 (Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical).

Agonist at the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors, producing anxiolytic, hypnotic, muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant effects; potency ~6–10 times diazepam. Receptor / target profile: Positive allosteric modulator at the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors; clinically regarded as a benzodiazepine.
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 0.5–2 h. Metabolised by CYP3A4 to active alpha-hydroxyetizolam. Half-life ~3.4 h (metabolite ~8 h).
Anxiety neurosis and generalised anxiety disorder (short-term)
Anxiety, tension and sleep disturbance in depression or psychosomatic disease
Anxiety: 0.5 mg two to three times daily (max 3 mg/day)
Insomnia: 1–3 mg at bedtime (lower doses are often adequate)
Limit treatment to 2–4 weeks; taper gradually
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Dependence and withdrawal – short-term use; taper
Somnolence, ataxia, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; flumazenil with caution.
Comparative randomised trials (e.g. versus alprazolam, mainly in India and Japan) show similar anxiolytic efficacy; long-term data limited.
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
